For each fixed \(n\), the number of \(r\in[0,n]\) with \(\binom nr\) odd is \(2^{\operatorname{popcount}(n)}\).

Thus the number of even binomial coefficients is
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{63}\left((n+1)-2^{\operatorname{popcount}(n)}\right).
\]
The total number of pairs is
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{63}(n+1)=\frac{64\cdot 65}{2}=2080.
\]
Since \(0\le n\le 63\) covers all 6-bit numbers,
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{63}2^{\operatorname{popcount}(n)}
=\sum_{k=0}^{6}\binom{6}{k}2^k
=3^6=729.
\]
Therefore the required count is
\[
2080-729=1351.
\]

\[
\boxed{1351}
\]
